Therapy, while helpful for some, often pathologizes and tries to “fix” people instead of truly holding space, especially around grief. Most therapists aren’t equipped to carry the weight of grief, especially cultural grief. That’s the gap I feel called to help bridge through my death and life work, to help guide people through the dark and create culturally competent spaces for transformation. We don’t do grief well as a society. We don’t show up well for each other. And I want to be part of changing that, of creating a future where we build tools, language, and etiquette for care. Not just healing for the individual, but healing that’s held and witnessed in community.
